<reason>Both sides argued competently and stayed disciplined on evidence, but PRO progressively narrowed the debate to a single decisive question and won it. By Rebuttal 2, CON had conceded registration, cameras, dwell limits, enforcement, and even fixed permit fees, leaving only whether the fee may vary by time and place. PRO's closing exposed the weakness of CON's late request-order reservation queue: at zero price, flexible vans have no reason to shift off 5pm, so the queue merely moves first-come allocation online and can still lock out the inflexible trip. CON's best line—that price rations by ability to pay rather than necessity—was legitimate and sharpened in the closing, but PRO had already pre-empted it (idling costs dwarf a small fee for commercial vans; caps/exemptions are allowed; motion says "allow"). CON's Q1 dilemma was sharp, but PRO's A1 ("rises until the marginal flexible stop leaves, then stops") plus CON's own admission that scarcity persists under either policy in the all-inflexible case produced PRO's clean "tie in the worst case, win everywhere else" weighing. PRO's two clipped turns were an execution cost, but the visible content was complete enough not to change the outcome.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's closing ([B5.1]-[B5.5]) stripping the clash to "may the fee vary?" and showing that CON's zero-price reservation queue gives the flexible van no reason to move, so only pricing distinguishes flexible from inflexible demand at 5pm.</best_rebuttal>
